supporting_role: high-fidelity hydrogen mixing and geometry evidence

target_questions.question: How do hydrogen properties, pressure ratio, and round/annular geometry alter mixing outside the shock-containing core?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 1 B028 links NPR/nozzle geometry to mixing; this LES study adds round-versus-annular and baroclinic interpretation.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: Validated LES indicates that hydrogen enhances mixing outside the jet core through baroclinic effects, while pressure ratio and round-versus-annular geometry reorganize coherent structures and mixture formation.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: PIV/schlieren validation and flow-structure analysis separate shock-core similarity from species- and geometry-dependent turbulent mixing.

limitations: Free nonreacting jets; baroclinic attribution is simulation-based and configuration-dependent.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
